habitat: Pairs and flocks at cliffs, caves or buildings, where they roost and breed, dispersing daily for fruit and berries.
summary: A common resident. The female has a grey head and mantle. Both sexes show brick-red flight feathers, which the description calls red-brown. The eye is dark. The most frequent call is a drawn-out spreeooo. The male's body colour is not stated. The Kemp name Redwinged Starling and the code RB were left unchanged.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The flight feathers are brick-red and red-brown, so no single wing colour is stored. The male body colour is not stated. The eye is only described as dark. The grade A call is from the Eastern Cape. The iNaturalist account has no display name, so the login tjeerd is credited. The Kemp name Redwinged Starling and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^12=4096 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 2048–8192.
